To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the number of developers is the most important factor that determines success, (2) the number of downloads and the number of users are also important factors that determine success, (3) the number of releases is an indicator for success, (4) the number of contributors is a negative indicator for success and (5) there is a positive relationship between the number of developers and number of downloads and between the number of contributors and number of downloads.
successful OSS projects tend to be: (1) small, with few contributors; (2) focused on one specific platform; (3) developed by a single developer; (4) written in a single programming language.
successful OSS projects tend to be: (1) large, (2) mature, (3) have a large number of developers, and (4) have a large user community.

the OSS community, in general, is more likely to be successful when it is more active, more responsive to users, and more collaborative.
